a2-n-lampe: It is dark in your room and you want to read. You press a switch on the small thing on your desk and it gives light.
In a furniture shop you look for something that hangs from the ceiling or stands on the floor and has a bulb inside.
Your friend visits and says it is too dark. You turn on the light on the table next to your bed. Which word means 'lamp'?
a2-v-traeumen: At night you sleep and see strange pictures in your head, for example you are flying over the sea.
In class you look out of the window and imagine a holiday on a beach far away instead of listening.
In the morning you tell your friend what happened in your head while you slept: you could fly! Which verb means 'to dream'?
a2-n-kalender: On the kitchen wall hangs a big sheet with all the days of the month. You write the dentist's appointment on it.
It is December and in a shop you buy a poster with twelve months for the new year.
You check on your phone which weekday the 15th is and add a meeting. Which word means 'calendar'?
a2-adj-wach: It is 3 a.m. and you cannot sleep. You lie in bed with your eyes open.
After a strong coffee in the morning you are no longer sleepy and your mind is clear.
Your baby sister was sleeping, but now her eyes are open and she looks around. Which word means 'awake'?
a2-adv-genug: The waiter offers you more rice, but your plate is already full. You say: 'No more, thanks, I have had ... '.
At the till you count your money: you need 10 euros and you have 12. You have all you need.
Your mother pours milk into your glass and you say stop when there is the right amount. Which word means 'enough'?
a2-n-stuhl: You come into the kitchen and sit down at the table, on a piece of furniture with four legs and a back, but no arms.
At a party there are not enough seats for everyone, so someone brings one more from the other room.
After class the teacher asks you to push this seat under the desk before you leave. Which word means 'chair'?
a2-n-ruhe: You live next to a busy road. On holiday in a mountain village you hear no cars and no voices, only birds.
Your neighbours are shouting in the hallway. You open the door and ask them politely for some quiet.
After a very hard week you lie on the sofa and do nothing at all. You feel calm and relaxed. What do you need now?
a2-v-tragen: It is cold outside, so you have a thick jacket and a scarf on your body.
Your neighbour has many heavy shopping bags. You help her bring them up the stairs in your hands.
A porter takes your suitcase from the train to the taxi, holding its weight. Which verb means 'to carry'?
a2-n-ahnung: A friend asks you for the capital of Mongolia and you know nothing at all. You shrug and say you have not got a clue.
You feel that something is wrong, but you cannot prove it. It is only a vague suspicion.
Your teacher asks if you know how the machine works. You shake your head: you do not have the faintest notion about it.
a2-adj-interessant: A film about deep-sea animals keeps you watching for two hours without looking at your phone.
Your classmate tells you a story about his trip that makes you want to hear more.
The book is not boring at all. Which word means 'interesting'?
a2-n-link: Your friend sends you a message with a blue underlined text. You tap it and a web page opens.
You want to share a funny video. You copy the web address and paste it into the chat.
An email says: 'Click on this to reset your password.' What do you click on?
a2-v-einpacken: Tomorrow you fly to Berlin. Tonight you put your clothes and shoes into the suitcase.
It is your friend's birthday. You cover the gift in colourful paper and tie a ribbon around it.
You buy a cake and the seller puts it in a box for you. Which verb means 'to pack'?
a2-n-ausstellung: On Sunday you go to a museum hall to look at paintings by a famous artist that are shown for two months.
Your class visits a place where cars from the 1950s are displayed for visitors to look at.
Your friend invites you to see her photos hanging on the walls of a small gallery. Which word means 'exhibition'?
a2-adv-dienstags: You go swimming every week on the second day of the working week, never on another day. Which adverb says this happens regularly on that day?
A sign at the market says that the stalls are open every week on the day after Monday, but not on the other days.
The bakery has its day off every week on the day between Monday and Wednesday. Which adverb means 'on Tuesdays'?
a2-n-interesse: You always read about planets and watch videos about space because it fascinates you. This curiosity about a topic is what?
In a job interview you are asked about your hobbies. You say you have a strong ... in photography.
A salesman shows you an expensive watch. You shake your head: you feel no wish to know more or to buy it.
a2-adj-schmutzig: You play football in the rain and come home with mud all over your trousers.
The kitchen window has not been washed for a year and you can hardly see through it.
Your hands are black after fixing your bike chain. Which word means 'dirty'?
a2-v-streiten: Two brothers shout at each other because both want the last piece of pizza.
At work two colleagues have different opinions and speak loudly and angrily about who made the mistake.
Your parents raise their voices about money in the kitchen. Which verb means 'to quarrel'?
a2-n-baecker: At six in the morning a man in a white apron takes fresh bread out of a hot oven. What is his job?
Every morning you go to a small shop on the corner to buy rolls and bread.
Your neighbour asks where you are going. You are heading to the place where bread is made and sold.
a2-n-festival: Every summer you camp for three days in a field and listen to many bands on big stages.
Your town has an open-air music weekend with food trucks, tents and thousands of young people.
A big event takes place in your city where new movies from many countries are shown over one week. Which word means 'festival'?
a2-n-erdgeschoss: You live in a building with four floors. Your friend lives on the level at the same height as the street, so he needs no stairs.
In the lift of a hotel you press the button marked 0 and arrive in the entrance hall.
Your grandmother cannot climb stairs, so she looks for a flat on the level at street height. Which word means 'ground floor'?
a2-adj-duenn: You spread butter on bread in a very flat layer, almost see-through.
It is winter, but your jacket is made of very light cloth and does not keep you warm.
Your friend has lost weight and now has a very narrow, slim body. Which word means 'thin'?
a2-v-schneien: You look out of the window in December and white flakes are falling from the sky. Everything outside turns white.
The weather forecast says it will be minus three degrees tomorrow and the children are excited because they might build a man from white flakes.
It is minus two degrees and the clouds are heavy and grey. Which verb means 'to snow'?
a2-adv-hinein: You stand outside a café with a friend and point through the door. You say: 'Let's go ...!' meaning 'in, into'.
You are outside by the door of the cellar and wave your friend toward the dark room: 'Come on, ...!'
You throw your dirty clothes into the washing machine. Which direction word, meaning 'into', describes this movement away from you?
a2-n-stueck: At a birthday party someone cuts a cake and gives you a slice. What do you get?
At the market the seller asks how much cheese you want. You ask for a small chunk cut from the big block.
You break your chocolate bar into parts and give one to your friend. Which word means 'piece'?
a2-n-wohnzimmer: In the evening the whole family sits on the sofa in front of the TV, in the main room of the flat where you relax.
Guests arrive. You take them into the room with the sofa and the coffee table, not into the kitchen.
You show a visitor around your flat: bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, and the largest room for relaxing and meeting guests. Which word means 'living room'?
a2-v-fallen: A glass slips from your hand and drops to the floor, where it breaks.
In autumn the leaves leave the tree and come down to the ground.
At night the temperature goes down from 15 to 5 degrees. Which verb describes this downward movement?
a2-n-autorin: You read a novel and look at the name of the woman who wrote it on the cover.
At a book reading in the library, a woman reads aloud from her own new book. Who is she?
Your teacher says: 'The writer of this story is a woman from Vienna.' Which word means 'author (female)'?
a2-adj-erkaeltet: You have a runny nose, you cough and you sneeze, so you stay at home and drink hot tea.
At the doctor's office he says: 'It is nothing serious, just a mild illness with a sore throat. Rest for a few days.'
Your colleague sneezes all day and has a red nose. You say: 'You look like you have a cold.' Which adjective means 'with a cold'?
a2-n-sache: Your friend asks what is wrong. You say it is a long story about one problem that must be solved: 'It is a difficult ...'
You cannot remember the name of an object on the shelf, so you say 'Give me that ... over there', using a general word for any object.
Your teacher says: 'This is a serious matter and we must talk about it.' Which general word means 'matter' or 'thing'?
a2-v-uebersetzen: You read a letter in a language you do not know, so you write each sentence again in your own language.
At a business meeting a man says every sentence from one language into another so the foreign guests understand.
You use an app on your phone to turn the menu text into your own language. Which verb means 'to translate'?
a2-n-geldboerse: At the till you take a small leather case out of your pocket that holds coins, notes and cards.
You lose your small case with money and ID on the bus and go to the lost property office.
For her birthday you give your mother a small holder for coins. Which word means 'wallet' or 'purse'?
a2-adv-vormittags: Your lessons start at eight and finish before lunch. Which word describes this time of the day, 'in the morning'?
A sign on a shop says it is open from 9 until noon and closed after that. Which adverb names this time of the day?
You tell your boss: 'Between nine and twelve every day I have meetings.' Which time adverb do you use for this part of the day?
a2-n-ausbildung: After school, Lena works three days a week in a bakery and goes to a vocational school for two days, for three years, to learn the job.
To become a nurse you spend years learning at a hospital and a school. What do you call this period of learning a profession?
Your uncle says: 'I want my son to get a proper vocational education before he starts working.'
a2-adj-natuerlich: The label on the juice says: no sugar, no colouring, no artificial flavours added. Everything comes from nature.
In the mountains there is a lake not made by humans; it formed by itself. What kind of lake is it?
Her hair colour is not dyed; it is how it was from birth. Which word means 'natural'?
a2-n-kamera: On holiday you want to take pictures of the beach, so you take out a device with a lens.
In the shopping mall, small devices on the ceiling film everyone for security.
On your phone you open the app to take a selfie. Which word means 'camera'?
a2-v-spazieren: After Sunday lunch your family leaves the house to move slowly and calmly through the park, with no hurry.
It is a sunny evening and you go along the river with your dog at a slow pace.
Your grandfather says: 'After dinner I always take a slow, relaxed stroll around the block.' Which verb is that?
a2-n-gesundheit: The doctor says: 'Eat well, sleep enough and do sports. It is good for your body.' What is she talking about?
You are never ill, you have energy and no pain. You say you are lucky to have good ...
The cigarette box warns you that smoking harms this. Which word means 'health'?
a2-n-schloss: You turn the key in the front door. The metal part in the door holds it shut.
On a school trip you visit a huge old building with towers where a king once lived.
You lose your key and cannot open the door. You call a locksmith to change the part inside the door that the key fits into.
a2-adj-romantisch: You have dinner by candlelight with your partner, with soft music and a view of the sea.
A small old town with narrow streets, flowers and a river looks like a picture from a postcard.
Your boyfriend gives you roses and writes you a love letter. Which word means 'romantic'?
a2-v-wegmachen: There is a red wine stain on the tablecloth, and you scrub until the mark is gone.
The child draws on the wall with a pen. Mum says: 'Clean that off right now!'
Your landlord asks you to take the old furniture out of the cellar and get rid of it. Which verb means 'to remove'?
a2-n-mailbox: You call your friend, but nobody answers. A voice asks you to leave a message after the beep.
Your email programme shows 253 new messages in the folder that collects everything sent to your address.
Your phone shows a small icon: two new recorded messages are waiting for you. Which word means 'voicemail'?
a2-adv-drinnen: It is pouring with rain, so the children play on the floor in the house, not in the garden.
The waiter asks if you want to sit in the garden or in the room. It is cold, so you choose the room.
Your friend asks: 'Is Tom in the garden?' You answer: 'No, he is in the house, not outside.' Which adverb means 'inside'?
a2-n-bewerbung: You want a new job, so you write a letter and send your CV to the company.
The university asks you to send in documents and a form to get a place to study there.
A company receives fifty of these from candidates for one job. Which word means 'application'?
a2-v-fuehlen: You put your hand on the radiator to find out if it is warm. Your skin gives you the information.
After a long run your legs are tired and your heart beats fast. You tell your friend how your body seems.
The doctor asks: 'How do you ... today?' Which verb means 'to feel'?
a2-n-lust: Your friend asks if you want to go to the cinema tonight. You say yes because it sounds nice and you have the wish to go.
It is raining and you stay at home because you do not feel like going out at all.
Someone says: 'I fancy a pizza right now.' Which noun means the 'desire' or wish to do something?
a2-adj-weich: You press your fingers into a fresh sponge cake. It gives way and is not hard at all.
Your cat's fur feels very gentle under your hand and not rough.
The pillow is not firm. It is the opposite of hard. Which word means 'soft'?
a2-n-projekt: At work your team plans a new app for six months, with goals, tasks and a deadline.
In school your group researches and prepares a presentation about rivers over several weeks.
Your uncle plans to build a garden house by himself in the summer. Which word means 'project'?
a2-n-fach: Your school timetable lists maths, history and art. Each of these is what?
In the fridge door there is a little compartment for the butter. What is this small section called?
At the swimming pool you put your things into a small numbered space with a door and take the key. What is that space called?
a2-v-sich-umziehen: You come home sweaty from sport and put on different, clean clothes.
You are going to a wedding after work, so you take off your work shirt and put on a suit in the office.
Before swimming you go into a small cabin and put on your swimsuit instead of your normal clothes. Which verb is that?
a2-adv-nachts: The streets are empty and dark and most people sleep. Which adverb says this happens regularly 'at night'?
A nurse works in the hospital during the dark hours, from 10 pm to 6 am.
Stars and the moon shine in the sky only at this time of day, when it is dark. Which adverb names it?
a2-n-bohne: In the garden you grow green pods that climb up a stick and have small seeds inside.
Your grandmother soaks small, oval, dried seeds overnight to cook a soup.
In a tin from the supermarket you find baked ones in tomato sauce. Which word means 'bean'?
a2-adj-geschieden: Your neighbour was married for ten years, but now her marriage has legally ended.
On a form a man ticks the box for a person whose marriage was officially ended by a court.
Your friend's parents no longer live together and a court has ended their marriage. Which word means 'divorced'?
a2-n-unfall: Two cars crash at a crossing. The police and an ambulance arrive.
A child falls off her bike and breaks her arm. Her parents say it was an unlucky event.
Your colleague is not at work because he hurt his leg when he slipped on the ice. Which word means 'accident'?
a2-v-merken: You leave the shop and suddenly realise that the cashier gave you too little change.
Your teacher says: 'Try to keep this phone number in your head until tomorrow.'
Your friend left the party early, but you only became aware of it an hour later. Which verb is that?
a2-n-training: Every Tuesday evening you go to the sports hall to practise with your football team and the coach.
In the gym you lift weights for an hour three times a week.
The marathon is in two months, so you run five times a week to prepare. Which word means 'workout' or 'practice'?
a2-n-handtuch: After a shower you dry your body with a big soft cloth.
At the pool you lay a big cotton cloth on the sunbed.
In a hotel bathroom there is none left, so you ask the reception for another one. Which word means 'towel'?
a2-adj-wirklich: The diamond in the ring is not a copy or made of glass. It is genuine.
A child sees a picture of a dragon and asks if it exists outside books. You say: 'No, it is not ...'
A man says: 'My ... name is Peter, but everyone calls me Pete.' He means his true name. Which word means 'real'?
a2-v-zeigen: A tourist asks for the way. You stretch out your arm and use your finger to direct her to the station.
At the end of your holiday you open your laptop and let your parents see the photos.
The teacher draws on the board how the machine works so the students can see it. Which verb means 'to show'?
a2-n-kaese: On a slice of bread you put a yellow, salty slice that is made from milk.
In a cartoon the little mouse is always looking for yellow, holey food made from milk.
At the dairy counter you ask for 200 grams of Gouda. Which word means 'cheese'?
a2-adv-donnerstags: Your choir practises every week on the day before Friday.
The market takes place weekly on the day between Wednesday and Friday.
You tell a colleague that you always work from home on the fourth day of the working week. Which adverb means 'on Thursdays'?
a2-n-latein: At school you study the old language of the Romans.
A doctor writes the names of illnesses in the ancient language of the Roman Empire.
In the old days you needed to know this dead language to study medicine. Which word means 'Latin'?
a2-n-bibliothek: You need a quiet place to study and to borrow books for free with a card.
At university you go to a big building with long shelves of books and reading tables to prepare for exams.
Your child wants a novel but you do not want to buy it. Where can you borrow it? Which word means 'library'?
a2-adj-heiss: You touch the cooker plate and burn your finger.
In July it is 38 degrees and everyone is sweating at the beach.
You pour boiling water on a teabag and the cup is too ... to drink. Which word means 'hot'?
a2-v-weitermachen: You are tired during a long walk and stop. Your friend says: 'Come on, do not stop now.'
A fire alarm interrupted the lesson. Afterwards the teacher says: 'Let's keep going with the exercise.'
You did half of your homework and want a break, but then decide to carry on. Which verb means 'to continue'?
a2-n-klassenfahrt: Your teacher takes the whole class by bus to a youth hostel by the sea for a week.
Parents must pay money and sign a form so their children can join a week away with their classmates.
You sleep in a room with five classmates in a hostel. Which word means 'school trip'?
a2-n-mathematik: In the classroom the teacher explains fractions, equations and geometry.
You have a test tomorrow with numbers, algebra and calculating angles.
Your sister loves numbers and wants to study this subject at university. Which word means 'maths'?
a2-v-basteln: Before Christmas the kids cut paper and glue stars to hang in the window.
Your father spends Sunday in the garage, building things from wood and wire with his hands.
In kindergarten the children make a card with scissors and glue. Which verb means 'to do handicrafts'?
a2-adv-anders: Your friend asked you to wear a green shirt, but you wore a blue one. You chose another colour than expected.
Two twins look alike, but each one thinks about things in a way that does not match the other.
Your boss says the plan failed, so next time you should try another way. Which adverb means 'differently'?
a2-n-kuenstler: A man paints large pictures and sells them in a gallery. What is he called?
On the street a man plays violin and paints portraits for passers-by.
Your uncle makes sculptures from metal and shows them in exhibitions. Which word means 'artist' (male)?
a2-adj-traurig: Your best friend moves to another country tomorrow. You cry and do not feel like talking.
You watch a film where the dog dies and your eyes get wet.
You failed your exam and you feel very down. Which word means 'sad'?
a2-n-nudel: You boil long thin strips of dough in salted water and serve them with tomato sauce.
In a soup, little yellow strings float next to chicken pieces.
You pick one long thin string out of the pot with a fork to test if it is soft. Which word means 'noodle'?
a2-v-ueben: To play the piano well, you play the same song every day for half an hour.
Before the driving test you drive around the car park again and again with the instructor.
Your teacher says: 'Repeat the words many times and you will learn them.' Which verb means 'to practise'?
a2-n-kunst: In school you have a lesson where you paint pictures and draw with coloured pencils.
In a museum you look at paintings, sculptures and old drawings.
Your friend says that music, painting and theatre are all forms of ... Which word means 'art'?
a2-n-rezept: You want to cook lasagne but do not know the amounts, so you look for the list of ingredients and steps in a cookbook.
You have a bad cough and the doctor writes a note so that the pharmacy gives you medicine.
Your grandmother's pancakes are famous and everyone asks her for the secret instructions. Which word means 'recipe'?
a2-adj-wahr: Your friend tells an unbelievable story and you ask if it really happened. He says: 'Yes, it is ...'
In a quiz you must say whether each sentence is correct or false: 'Paris is the capital of France.' You tick the right box.
A story is not made up; it is how it really happened. Which word means 'true'?
a2-n-onkel: Your mother's brother comes to visit with a present.
Your father's brother lives in Hamburg and has two sons, your cousins.
At a family party you point to the man who is the brother of one of your parents. Which word means 'uncle'?
a2-v-braten: In a pan with oil you cook a steak until it is brown on both sides.
On Sunday your mother puts a chicken in the oven for two hours until it is golden.
You heat oil in a pan and put in eggs and potatoes. Which verb means 'to fry'?
a2-adv-hinaus: From inside the house you point to the garden door and tell the dog: 'Go ...!' meaning 'out'.
At the end of the meeting the boss opens the door and tells the people to leave the room.
You stand on the balcony and throw a ball away from the room. Which direction word means 'out'?
a2-n-insel: On holiday you take a ferry to a piece of land that is completely surrounded by water.
Robinson was alone on a piece of land in the sea with no other people.
Mallorca is a piece of land in the sea. Which word means 'island'?
a2-n-weg: A tourist asks how to get to the station and you explain which streets to follow.
A narrow track in the forest leads to a lake. Hikers follow it on foot.
On your way home you take a shortcut. Which word means 'path' or 'way'?
a2-adj-fit: You run 5 km three times a week and can climb stairs without getting out of breath.
Your grandfather is 80 but still rides a bike every day and feels strong and healthy.
After your illness the doctor says you can do sport again because your body is in good shape. Which word means 'fit'?
a2-v-hoffen: Tomorrow is your exam. You cannot do anything more, but you wish very much that it goes well.
Your friend is ill. You think and wish that she gets better soon.
It is cloudy, but you want the sun to come out for the picnic. Which verb means 'to hope'?
a2-n-verspaetung: The train should have arrived at 8:00 but only comes at 8:20. The sign says twenty minutes more than planned.
Your colleague arrives at the meeting fifteen minutes after the start and says sorry.
The announcement at the airport says flight 123 will leave later than planned. Which word means 'delay'?
a2-n-pferd: At the farm a big brown animal with a mane and four legs pulls a cart.
Girls in riding boots sit on large animals in the riding school and jump over bars.
A cowboy in a film rides one through the desert. Which word means 'horse'?
a2-v-interessieren: Your friend shows you a documentary about volcanoes. You say it makes you curious and you want to know more: 'It ... me.'
Football does not catch your attention at all, but music does.
Your teacher tells stories to make the class curious about history. Which verb means 'to interest'?
a2-n-fest: In summer the whole village meets in the main square with music, beer tents and fireworks.
At Christmas the family has a big meal together with presents and singing. This special occasion is what?
Your neighbours invite everyone to a big party in the garden. Which word means 'celebration'?
a2-adj-getrennt: At the restaurant the waiter asks: 'Together or ...?' Each person pays their own bill.
The couple still like each other but live in two different flats, apart from one another.
You put paper in one bin and plastic in another, so the two kinds of waste are kept apart. Which word means 'separate'?
a2-adv-natuerlich: A friend asks: 'Can you help me move on Saturday?' You answer with a cheerful word meaning 'sure, no problem'.
Someone asks: 'Do you know Berlin?' You lived there for ten years: '... I know it well!'
Someone asks if you like ice cream on a hot day and you say yes, as is obvious. Which adverb means 'of course'?
a2-n-zettel: Before you go to the supermarket you write what you need on a small sheet of paper.
Your flatmate leaves a short message on the fridge saying he went to work.
After paying at the shop the cashier gives you a small printed sheet that shows what you bought. Which word means 'piece of paper' or 'receipt'?
a2-n-markt: On Saturday morning you buy fresh vegetables from stalls in the town square.
Farmers sell apples and eggs from small stands under umbrellas.
At Christmas you drink hot spiced wine at a place with wooden huts in the town centre. Which word means 'market'?
a2-v-organisieren: You plan a surprise party: you book a room, order a cake and invite the guests.
At work you have to make sure that the meeting room, the projector and the coffee are ready.
Your class goes on a trip and the teacher says: 'Who wants to arrange the tickets?' Which verb means 'to organize'?
a2-n-gitarre: At a campfire someone plays songs on an instrument with six strings.
A rock musician plays loudly on a stage with an electric one.
You start lessons to learn an instrument with a wooden body, a neck and strings. Which word means 'guitar'?
a2-adj-frisch: At the market the vegetables were picked this morning and still look crisp.
You open the window in the morning and the air is cool and clean.
The bread has just come out of the oven and is not old. Which word means 'fresh'?
a2-n-spiel: Children sit on the floor and move pieces on a board, rolling dice.
On Saturday your football team plays against another team and it ends 2:1.
On the phone your little brother plays an electronic one for hours. Which word means 'game'?
a2-v-bestehen: You studied hard for the driving test and got the result you needed. You succeeded.
The teacher asks what water is made of. You say: 'It ... of hydrogen and oxygen.'
The company was founded in 1900 and is still here today. Which verb means 'to exist'?
a2-adv-weg: You come back to your desk and your phone is not there. It has disappeared.
A friend leaves on holiday for two weeks. He is not here, he is gone.
You say to a fly: 'Go ...!' Which adverb means 'away'?
a2-n-grippe: You have a high fever, aching muscles and chills for a week. The doctor says a virus caused it and you must stay in bed.
In autumn the doctor offers a vaccination against a winter virus that makes many people absent from the office.
You feel terrible, with a fever and body aches. Which noun means 'flu'?
a2-n-zitrone: In your tea you squeeze a sour yellow fruit.
You make a cold drink with sugar, water and the juice of a sour yellow fruit.
At the market you buy a yellow citrus fruit that is very sour. Which word means 'lemon'?
a2-adj-sauber: You mop the floor and wipe the table until there is no dust left.
After washing your hands with soap they look and smell fresh.
The hotel room was spotless, with no stain anywhere. Which word means 'clean'?
a2-v-sich-beschweren: Your soup arrives cold. You call the waiter and tell him you are unhappy about it.
Your neighbours play loud music at 2 a.m., so you go to the landlord and say it is not acceptable.
The hotel room was dirty, so you write to the manager to say how unhappy you are. Which verb means 'to complain'?
